source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Classify straight-line motion as uniform or non-uniform from equal time intervals.

intelligence.enrichment: An object moving along a straight line at constant speed is in uniform linear motion and covers equal distances in equal time intervals; if its speed changes, it is in non-uniform linear motion and covers unequal distances in equal time intervals. Equal distance increments over equal time intervals show constant speed; unequal distance increments over equal time intervals show changing speed. The learner correctly applies this rule: An object moving along a straight line at constant speed is in uniform linear motion and covers equal distances in equal time intervals; if its speed changes, it is in non-uniform linear motion and covers unequal distances in equal time intervals. Straight-line motion is uniform just because it stays on one straight track, regardless of the distance covered in each equal time interval.
